title: Poyhas Swamp
summary: Poyhas is recorded as a swamp within the Hashamomuk bounds in Southold. The place is connected with Poyhas, a Native person who lived and planted there.
history_content: Poyhas Swamp was reserved within the Hashamomuk Neck landscape. Dated source details appear in the Historic Timeline with their own references.
translation_content:
No separate linguistic translation is given for Poyhas. The name is treated as a personal name attached to a swamp reserved for Poyhas within Hashamomuk bounds.

Why Place Names Matter

“Origin stories about place-names are themselves a form of myth and folktale—perhaps inaccurate, but interesting in their own right because they record people's beliefs about place names even when those beliefs lack factual grounding.”

— William Cronon, Names on the Land: Place Names as Historical Evidence (2018), Section I, paragraph beginning “This should remind you”
preservation_content: Poyhas preserves a named planting and dwelling place inside the larger Hashamomuk landscape, showing that smaller swamps, fields, and reserved places remained important within broader land transactions.
